explanations: Intel 12th and 13th gen CPUs both use LGA 1700, so the upgrade works. AMD Ryzen 7000 uses AM5, a completely different socket with no cross-platform compatibility. Review: Chapter 1, Motherboards, Processors, and Memory (CPU sockets, LGA 1700, AM5).

USB 3.2 Gen 2 ports run at 10 Gbps and are typically color-coded teal (or red on some boards), distinct from USB 3.0's blue. The port shape is the same Type-A, but the color coding helps technicians identify the faster standard. Review: Chapter 3, Peripherals, Cables and Connectors (USB generations, color coding, data transfer rates).

chkdsk /f scans the volume for file system errors and fixes them. The /f switch specifically repairs file system errors (versus /r which also checks for bad sectors). Must run from an elevated command prompt and may require a reboot for the system drive. Review: Chapter 2, Storage Devices and Power Supplies (disk maintenance, chkdsk switches).

RAID 5 uses striping with distributed parity across all drives. With four 2 TB drives, you get 6 TB usable (n−1). It tolerates one drive failure and provides good read performance. RAID 10 offers better write performance but only yields 4 TB (50% usable). The requirement to maximize capacity while maintaining redundancy makes RAID 5 the best choice. Review: Chapter 2, Storage Devices and Power Supplies (RAID levels, parity, stripe sets).

TPM (Trusted Platform Module) 2.0 is required for Windows 11 and is often disabled by default in BIOS. It is found in the Security section. TPM enables BitLocker drive encryption, Secure Boot attestation, and platform integrity. On Intel boards it may be labeled "Intel PTT"; on AMD, "fTPM". Review: Chapter 1, Motherboards, Processors, and Memory (BIOS/UEFI settings, TPM, security features).

System File Checker (sfc /scannow) scans all protected Windows system files and replaces corrupted or missing files with cached copies from the component store. Must be run elevated. If sfc cannot repair files, run DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth first. Review: Chapter 11, Troubleshooting Methodology (Windows recovery tools, sfc, DISM).

The seven steps of laser printing: (1) Processing: printer rasterizes data, (2) Charging: drum gets uniform negative charge, (3) Exposing: laser writes image by discharging areas, (4) Developing: toner adheres to discharged areas, (5) Transferring: toner moves to paper, (6) Fusing: heat and pressure bond toner, (7) Cleaning: residual toner removed from drum. Review: Chapter 4, Printers and Multifunction Devices (laser imaging process).

A yellow triangle (exclamation mark) in Device Manager indicates a device problem, typically a missing, corrupt, or incompatible driver. Right-click the device and select "Update driver" to search automatically or browse for a downloaded driver. If that fails, try uninstalling and rebooting to trigger PnP reinstallation. Review: Chapter 3, Peripherals, Cables and Connectors (Device Manager, driver troubleshooting).

diskpart is the Windows command-line disk partitioning utility. A new drive visible in BIOS but not in File Explorer needs initialization, partitioning, and formatting. After launching diskpart, use "list disk" to find the drive, "select disk N", "create partition primary", and "format fs=ntfs quick". Disk Management (diskmgmt.msc) provides a GUI alternative. Review: Chapter 2, Storage Devices and Power Supplies (diskpart, disk initialization, partition management).

While both DDR4 and DDR5 desktop DIMMs have 288 pins, the key notch is in a different position, making them physically incompatible. DDR4 operates at 1.2V while DDR5 runs at 1.1V with an on-die PMIC. DDR5 also starts at 4800 MT/s (vs DDR4's 2133 MT/s) and doubles bank groups. Review: Chapter 1, Motherboards, Processors, and Memory (RAM types, DDR4 vs DDR5, form factors, notch positions).
